ai.title: Add placeholder detection to file rewriting
ai.summary: Backend file processing now detects missing `... existing code ...` placeholders in single-function edits and triggers a `fastRewrite` with injected context. `processFileBlock` receives `messages` and `fullResponse` to run `shouldAddFilePlaceholders` logic. Updated `main-prompt.ts` and `process-file-block.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant rewrites a single function in a file, it now checks whether you forgot to leave the '... existing code...' placeholder that marks where the rest of the file should stay. If that placeholder is missing, the system automatically adds the surrounding context before rewriting, so the rest of your file doesn't get accidentally dropped. You'd notice this if you've ever lost code when asking for a small edit; now the system catches that mistake and protects your file. This is already active today.

ai.title: Strengthen placeholder comment guidance in system prompt
ai.summary: System prompt in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` now explicitly instructs the agent to abridge file content using placeholder comments to minimize written lines. Previous wording permitted but did not strongly encourage this behavior for unchanged code sections. This change aims to improve clarity and conciseness of edit blocks.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes code edits, it now gets a clearer instruction to keep unchanged parts of a file as short placeholder comments instead of retyping everything. The guidance changed from 'you can use placeholders' to 'you should use placeholders and try to write as few lines as possible.' If you looked at how edits are produced, you'd see the assistant leaning harder on placeholder comments to trim the size of each edit block. This is live today and affects how the assistant communicates code changes, not how the code itself runs.

ai.title: Prevent cookie banner visibility
ai.summary: CookieConsentCard.tsx now prevents the consent banner from appearing. The `setVisible(true)` logic based on localStorage is commented out. This effectively hides the UI element for all users.

eli5.text: The cookie consent banner that normally pops up to ask if you accept cookies will no longer appear the next time you visit the site. The team disabled the logic that displays the banner based on whether you previously accepted or declined cookies, so the prompt is now hidden for all visitors. Right now you would only notice its absence: pages load without the usual "We use cookies" message and Accept/Decline buttons at the bottom. This change is live today for everyone who comes to the site.

ai.title: Centralize spinner and update status messages
ai.summary: Introduce `Spinner` singleton in `npm-app/src/utils/spinner.ts` to manage CLI loading states. Replace ad-hoc intervals in `cli.ts` and `client.ts` with `Spinner.get().start/stop`. Update backend status strings in `main-prompt.ts` and sync Web demo copy in `InteractiveTerminalDemo.tsx`.

eli5.text: When the assistant is busy thinking or working behind the scenes, you’ll now see a smooth spinning indicator instead of inconsistent or missing loading messages. The program now uses one shared spinner component across the command-line tool and web demo, so loading states appear reliably whether you’re in the terminal or trying the interactive demo online. You won’t see random pauses or flickering messages anymore, just a clean spinning icon that disappears once the work is done.

ai.title: browseraction prompt adds XML examples
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts updated with explicit XML tag examples for browser_action types (navigate, type, scroll, screenshot). Includes strict instruction to use XML tags exclusively, prohibiting JSON or other formats. Internal change affecting agent behavior via system prompt only.

eli5.text: The assistant that controls the browser now gets clearer instructions showing exactly how to write commands for navigating, typing, scrolling, and taking screenshots. Instead of guessing the right format, it receives working examples that always use the same XML-style tags, and a note telling it not to mix in JSON or other formats. This change only affects how the assistant is taught to behave behind the scenes.

ai.title: Replace kill-port with native lsof/kill in dev script
ai.summary: The `dev` script in `backend/package.json` now uses `lsof -t -i:4242 | xargs kill -9` instead of the `kill-port` dependency to free port 4242. This removes the `kill-port` package from `devDependencies`. The change simplifies the dev startup sequence by relying on standard Unix utilities rather than a third-party tool.

eli5.text: The dev tool that starts your local backend server no longer relies on a small helper package to shut down whatever is already running on port 4242. Instead, it uses the operating system's built-in commands to find and stop that process. You won't see this unless you're starting the backend locally, but the startup command is slightly more reliable and no longer depends on that removed package.
